purpose: The FR-GOV-004 audit's findings. Every landed requirement that this repository cannot show delivered, and that no open partial closure covers, is classified here with the reasoning that justified the classification. Written at M4-C, where FR-GOV-004's wider audit came due after being deferred from M4-B so that it would not expand the slice that was writing payment capture.
how_to_read: state ABSENT means the behaviour genuinely does not exist: a product gap, and the only kind that can be a money, security or authority absence. state UNCITED means the behaviour exists and works and no recorded output names the requirement, so the audit cannot see the proof: a governance gap. Conflating the two inflates the urgent list until nobody reads it, so tools/requirement_coverage.py refuses an entry that pairs uncited with a money, security or authority category.
the_review_may_challenge_a_classificatio: THE M4 REVIEW MAY CHALLENGE ANY CLASSIFICATION AS READILY AS ANY FIX. A gap wrongly called schedulable is worse than one honestly called urgent, and the triage below is a judgement made by the builder under the deadline of a closing gate — which is exactly the condition under which 'not really a money gap' is an easy sentence to write. Each entry carries its reasoning so that the judgement can be read and disagreed with, and every entry is marked challengeable.
completing_gates_are_derived: completing_gate is the next gate at which the PACKAGE itself revalidates the requirement, taken from revalidated_at, or the final gate when there is none. Overridden only where this slice genuinely delivers the missing half, and those overrides all name M4-C. revalidated_at is reproduced on each entry so a reader can check the derivation without opening the package.

gaps.title: Golden journeys
gaps.why: The journeys exist, run in CI on both platforms and fail the build: five golden journeys, 61 steps. What the clause asks for and does not exist is the MAPPING artifact — every mandatory journey against test IDs, evidence, owner and defect status. gaps.title: Branding
gaps.why: Branding is configurable — config.configuration_version carries a branding category and the API resolves it per tenant rather than from build-time constants — but the clause names receipt and footer text specifically, and the package places its revalidation at M4 because receipt text is only rendered on a real receipt. There is no receipt at M4-B, so that clause has never been exercised. M4-C's receipt renders it and closes this.
gaps.buildable_why: BUILDABLE NOW, AND NOT BUILT. An earlier draft of this entry said 'built by this slice', which was false: no branding is rendered onto a receipt. Tenant branding configuration exists and the receipt composer exists; nothing joins them.
gaps.closes_when: A receipt renders its footer and branding text from configuration rather than a constant, in all three locales.

moved_later.why: The receipt is the artifact this clause names, and M5a is the gate that next opens the receipt composition path — it owns the outlet node and the print stage the composer feeds. Branding text pulled from configuration is a change to that composer, and doing it inside a repair brief would be building a feature under the word 'repair'. It was NOT built at M4-C and this entry was stale, not satisfied.

gaps.what_would_make_it_buildable: docs.compose_document() would read the tenant's branding category from config.configuration_version and emit it as header and footer wording, and a control would prove one tenant's text appears on its own receipt and never on another's. Nothing blocks that today. Re-pointing this to M5a is a PREFERENCE, not a constraint — M5a is simply where the outlet node makes branding per-outlet.
